source_message:
feat: BANXE AML block runtime — 3-layer collective LexisNexis stack

Phase 3: tx_monitor.py — 9 rules, score_transaction() → list[RiskSignal],
  imports thresholds/jurisdictions from compliance_validator (Layer 1),
  Redis velocity, legacy check_transaction() backward-compat wrapper.

Phase 4: sanctions_check.py — stdlib urllib (no httpx), difflib fallback,
  SanctionsSubject input, list[RiskSignal] output, SANCTIONS_CONFIRMED/
  PROBABLE/SUBJECT_JURISDICTION_A/B rules.

Phase 5: crypto_aml.py — stdlib urllib (no httpx, no FINOS OpenAML),
  WalletScreeningInput input, list[RiskSignal] output, CRYPTO_SANCTIONS/
  CRITICAL/HIGH_RISK/ELEVATED/HIGH_VALUE rules.

Phase 2: models.py — shared data contracts: TransactionInput,
  SanctionsSubject, WalletScreeningInput, CustomerProfile,
  RiskSignal, AMLResult.

Phase 6: aml_orchestrator.py — generic Layer 2 aggregator,
  assess(tx, subject, wallet) → AMLResult, hard override rules.

Phase 3b: banxe_aml_orchestrator.py — Layer 3 BANXE runtime,
  banxe_assess(transaction, customer, counterparty, wallet, channel)
  → BanxeAMLResult with case_id, policy_version, signal-priority
  decision engine (hard overrides + high-risk floor), to_api_response()
  and to_audit_dict() for ClickHouse insert.

Phase 7: COMPLIANCE_ARCH.md — Phase 16, 3-layer ASCII diagram,
  directory layout, example flow, signal-priority vs pure summation table.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
